title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 59 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: drones & air autonomy and allies & theaters.

stories.h: DOW Advances Seven Laser Teams to Phase II Counter-Drone Shoot-Off
stories.what: JIATF 401 has picked Lockheed Martin, Kord, AeroVironment and four others for mid-December live-fire drone trials.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: LeoLabs acquires FishEye to bolster its missile defense chops
stories.what: “As a wholly owned subsidiary of LeoLabs, FishEye will strengthen our ability to accelerate delivery of our next-generation radars optimized for missile warning and tracking, such as Scout-X,” a LeoLabs spokesperson told Breaking Defense.
stories.you: Missile defense is one of the biggest budget lines this decade, and its software and sensors are open to newcomers.

stories.h: SpaceNukes Opens Los Alamos Manufacture and Materials Facility to Build Its Next-Generation Space Reactor
stories.what: LOS ALAMOS, N.M., Nov. 16, 2026 — Space Nuclear Power Corp. (SpaceNukes) opened its Manufacture and Materials Development Facility at 150 Central Park Square in Los Alamos on Nov. 13. [ ]
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: Why the Pentagon Wants to Spend $2B in FY27 to Develop Directed Energy Weapons
stories.what: The Pentagon is pouring $2 billion into the development of directed energy weapons that can counter drone swarms and other threats.
stories.you: Stopping cheap drones cheaply is the industry's most urgent problem and one of its fastest-growing markets.

stories.h: Senate appropriators unveil $1.1T Pentagon spending bill, folding in reconciliation priorities
stories.what: Nearly $69 billion in money sought by the White House through reconciliation will be rolled into the base budget under the Senate appropriator’s plan.
stories.you: Budget and policy moves decide which programs get real money and when; they're the earliest signal of demand.

watch.h: Stopgap funding expires: FY27 appropriations or another CR
watch.why: December 11. Decides whether DAWG's $54.6B and Golden Dome's growth become real money.

idea.why: Motors using ferrite or reluctance designs, or recycled magnets, for small drones and actuators. China controls heavy rare earths. A compliant motor is a chokepoint product every drone maker needs.
